text:
Alice M.: Heads up — saw a CPU-side perf regression on the token pipeline after last night's canary. GPU looks fine in nsys, but perf flame shows much more time in the Python scheduler + tokenizer handoff than before. attaching quick flame.svg
Ben (eng-runtime): Can you paste the perf commands you ran?
Alice M.: Sure — I recorded system-wide stacks for 30s on the canary box
```
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
Top-level rough breakdown from folded counts: tokenization: ~43% | scheduler/batcher code (python) ~27% | kv_cache lookup/syscall ~9% | syscall:read+recv ~7% | gc/alloc ~4% | misc C++ runtime ~10%
Carol S.: That scheduler chunk looks like GIL handoff / thread wakeups. Did we change the batching heuristic recently?
Alice M.: Yes — we switched to the new "batch_shift" heuristic in deploy abc123. Config snippet:
```
batching:
  heuristic: batch_shift
  flush_interval_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
```
After the change throughput improved on short sequences but CPU time per token jumped on long-run QA workloads.
Dave R.: I repro'd locally and saw repeated calls into our Python kv cache wrapper that do small reads -> syscall churn. snippet from strace showed many read(3, .., 128) calls. Looks like buffer sizing + handoff causing syscalls rather than memcpy.
Ben (eng-runtime): Any chance the kernel selection changes bumped a small-IO codepath? Or the prefetch thread interaction changed?
Alice M.: Kernel selection didn't change. But batch_shift causes more frequent premature flushes, so many small prefix cache lookups happen. Those go through the Python wrapper before C++ fast path. I'll paste the minimal repro I used:
```
# repro script
python -c "from runtime import Client; c=Client();
for _ in range(2000):
  c.generate('x'*1200)
"
```
perf-bot: nsys timeline snippet: GPU busy 38%, idle 62% during the window; CPU queues show increased wakeups coincident with batch flushes.
Carol S.: Two quick experiments: 1) pin runtime threads to cores (taskset) to prove wakeup noise; 2) run with PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG or enable the C++ fast-path for kv cache to see delta.
Dave R.: I toggled the kv fast-path in my build and the tokenization scheduler drop went from 27% -> 9% (rough numbers). So it's the Python handoff + small lookups. Patch in flight to ensure cache lookup uses the fast C++ path if batch size < threshold.
Alice M.: Thanks — I'll revert batch_shift on canary and open an RFC/PR to add a guard so we don't regress long-run CPU. Creating PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimelib/pull/4826 — will run full perf + flamegraphs after the revert.
Ben (eng-runtime): Nice triage. After PR lands let's run a perf compare job (before/after) with the same seed to get numbers.
Alice M.: Will do. Saving flame + folded outputs in the bug: https://redwood.storage/perf/1977804321/
Carol S.: Awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:
